There's first, second, third-rate cannon fodder.
Can use sword qi: peak realm
Can use enhanced qi: transcendent realm

Thats's it for realms. The differences in strength between people in the same peak realm can be huge. The kids are at the lower end of peak realm, Namgung Su is at the upper end, and Mae Geuklyom around mid-upper. Ak Yeonho would be around the middle.

The difference is: 
1) The kids can emit sword qi or the like if they focus, but are incapable of using it in combat except as a finishing move.
2) Yeonho can consistently coat his spear in qi throughout a battle, from start to end.
3) Namgung Su is on the verge of being able to form enhanced qi, but can't do it consistently or use it in battle yet.
4) Suryong can freely wield enhanced qi in battle, but not for long.
5) Murim Alliance Chairman can spam enhanced qi however he wants.

Beyond realms, other factors like skill, physical condition, mental condition, technique, experience, and strategy come into play. That's why Grandpa can say he'll replace his fading physical strength and stamina with experience and resolve.

Chaos demon is interesting because "primordial chaos" can be interpreted as Wuji, the infinite undefined "something" that existed before and gave birth to the universe. Chaos demon should have been born from an experiment to practice Yin and Yang chi in one body. If his martial arts could encapsulate Wuji as a whole, it could definitely counter shadow, though, so he should be practicing just an aspect of it, the "hell demon" part of his cultivation technique. The spinning wind, regeneration, and murderous madness aspects might be expressions that the form it takes is of a self contained circle of life and death, spinning into a vortex.
The rebound, corruption, and targeted evolution aspects should also be linked closely together. The corruption and targeted evolution aspects are probably actually the same thing, it's just a matter of whose body the chi is transforming in. Rebound is conceptually very close to reflection, and it's confused by other experts apparently being able to do something similar, but I think what he does is closer to taking a physical imprint of his opponents chi. He doesn't even need to do anything, since his chi can contain anything, letting someone else's chi impact his will automatically leave behind a "negative" of the opponent's chi that can be materialized into an "antibody" that can cancel out the original chi. This is similar to some explanations of "karma" I've seen that focus on the causality facet of it, which in terms of imagery, suits a "demon of the underworld."
As for why the shadow slash worked on him? Although it's tempting to just say that you can't take an imprint of a shadow, a reflection is similarly immaterial and he was able to counter that, so in the interest of that pet theory I'd rather believe it's actually because of the sword technique rather than the cultivation one. After all, it's a sword that cuts through the heavens(pinnacle yang) and devils(pinnacle yin.) Rather than leaving a chi imprint that could become an antibody, the shadow slash cut a hole through the chi directly, primordial chaos or not.

Rather than a broad statement about martial arts, it's just that your personal martial art dao is based on the Taiji.

It is not wrong, it's just how it's translated into English to give context and understanding that it is the circular hollow disc shaped throwing weapon.
The root word in sanskrit चक्र (Cakra) is extremely broad, and literally just means wheel, disk, circle etc. Lexically it can have multiple literal and metaphorical uses.
However when translated there is no cultural context behind the word, so there is a need for a specific word to be created so as remove the need for context.
As it is, Chakra (English) refers to a concept in meditation practices, and Chakra (weapon) is assigned the name Chakra(m) so as to distinguish two distinct concepts that do not exist in the english lexicon.
So your indian editor and readers are correct... if the word were to be translated into an indian language.
Just like how 輪 in chinese is very broad and you decided there was a need to use Chakra(m) instead of Wheel in your translation to provide specific context, removing the M from chakram just removes that context from the understanding of english readers.
